ready1_open_rewrite.title: GeoSQA Open-ended Question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The Dengfeng County Astronomical Observatory in Henan (113°E, 34°N) is the earliest existing ancient astronomical observatory building in China. There are two small houses on the Astronomical Observatory, with a crossbeam between the small houses, and a “long embankment” directly north below the platform (see the figure below). Every day at noon, the shadow of the crossbeam will fall on the “long embankment”; using it, one can understand the changes of the starry sky in the four seasons. Read the graphic and textual materials and, combined with <image1>, answer: When the daily projection of the crossbeam on the long embankment is closest to the Astronomical Observatory, is the time earlier or later than Beijing time 12:00?

Therefore, local noon occurs at about Beijing time 12:28, so it is later than Beijing time 12:00.
